subject.title: feat(google-meet): retain the full caption transcript per session (#103387)

question: After final-window capture and explicit eviction signaling are fixed, should Google Meet transcripts remain bounded in process memory or become a durable SQLite-backed artifact?
rationale: Restart persistence and post-meeting history are user-visible data-lifetime semantics; repository policy establishes SQLite as the durable-state path but cannot decide whether this feature should intentionally remain ephemeral.

options.title: Bounded memory with explicit loss
options.body: Keep the fixed caps, expose every unavailable or evicted state clearly, document them, and require live proof of the complete lifecycle.

options.title: Durable SQLite artifact
options.body: Persist transcript history across gateway restarts and session churn before exposing post-meeting retrieval as a supported contract.

options.title: Active-session retrieval only
options.body: Remove post-meeting retention from this PR and defer historical transcripts to a separately designed durable artifact.

recommendation.title: Bounded memory with explicit loss
recommendation.body: Keep the fixed caps, expose every unavailable or evicted state clearly, document them, and require live proof of the complete lifecycle.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged history most strongly connects @steipete to the Google Meet runtime and original transcribe-caption feature.
